labels.rationale: ChatView subscribes to `chatState$[agentKey].transcript`, and every streamed chunk replaces that array (lib/chat-state.ts:315, :319), so the whole view, including the ThinkingOrb, the model Dropdown and ChatComposer, rerenders per token. Only ChatTranscript and SessionRail render the items; the owner needs the busy-tool flag and `transcript.length` (lines 175, 178-180), which merged chunks leave unchanged. The dynamic-key binding `chatState$[agentKey]` at line 149 is not proven, so no narrowing is offered.

The 1,560-line TerminalSurface subscribes to the whole document and actor refs (lines 724-725) only to derive `claimedTask` at line 726, read at 1909-1916 and 2079-2088. PersistentTerminalHost passes `node` from `terminal$.openByNodeId` and never subscribes to the document, so every document commit rerenders every open terminal; a selector returning the claimed task's id, sink and brief would rerender only when the claim changes.

`use$(terminal$.railsOpenByNodeId)` subscribes to every node's rails, but the surface reads only its own entry through actorRailsOpen (line 1796) and uses `.connections` at line 2187. A rail toggle on one terminal (lib/terminal-state.ts:127) rerenders every open TerminalSurface; subscribing to `railsOpenByNodeId[node.id]` limits it to the toggled one.

CanvasChrome subscribes to the whole document to pass `nodes.length > 0` to CanvasEmpty; App does not subscribe to the document, so every commit rerenders CanvasChrome, FilterTray and CanvasEmpty. Selecting the boolean rerenders only when the canvas gains or loses its first non-group node. The seed is the module constant EMPTY_DOC, which blocks the plain-seed proof.

App subscribes to `canvasName` only for the boot gate `booting && !canvasName` at line 562, so every canvas open (App.tsx:151, :186, :242) rerenders the root component and every unmemoized host under it. Selecting the combined boolean from `booting` and `canvasName` rerenders App only when the boot indicator appears or disappears.

syncChatCoarse writes `chatCoarse$[agentKey]` in place (lib/chat-state.ts:428, :440), so `use$(chatCoarse$)` returns the same record and the occupancy memo at line 79, keyed on `[doc, chatCoarse, ranked]`, keeps stale marks. Chat status, turnBusy and hasBusyTools flips come from chat events that write neither the document nor `ranked`, so the staffing marks stay wrong until the next document commit. The analyzer reports this as a candidate.
